([[Leetsdale, Pennsylvania]]) | college = [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] (2022–2024)
[[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]] (2024–2025) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | draft_league = | career_start = | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = | bbr = }} '''Adou Thiero''' (born May 8, 2004) is an American [[college basketball]] player for the [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas Razorbacks]] of the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC). He previously played for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]]. ==Early life== Thiero was born on May 8, 2004 in [[Utah]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.proballers.com/basketball/player/257960/adou-thiero|website=Proballers.com|title=Adou Thiero}}{{Cite web |date=2024-05-22 |title=Adou Thiero |url=https://arkansasrazorbacks.com/roster/adou-thiero/ |access-date=2025-01-17 |website=Arkansas Razorbacks |language=en-US}} His parents, Almamy and Mariam, immigrated to the U.S. from [[Mali]] and both played [[college basketball]]; his father, Almamy, for [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]] under coach [[John Calipari]] and then for [[Duquesne Dukes men's basketball|Duquesne]], while his mother, Mariam, for [[Oklahoma City Stars women's basketball|Oklahoma City]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.timesonline.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball/2022/04/28/adou-thiero-quaker-valley-quakers-division-i-basketball-recruit-kentucky-wildcats-almamy-thiero-mali/65350904007/|newspaper=[[The Beaver County Times]]|title=Adou Thiero's parents came to America to chase a dream. Now he has his own bright future|author=Upadhyaya, Parth|date=April 28, 2022}} His mother was selected in the [[2006 WNBA draft]] by the [[Washington Mystics]].{{Cite news|url=https://tribhssn.triblive.com/quaker-valleys-adou-thiero-named-2022-triblive-hssn-boys-basketball-player-of-the-year/|newspaper=[[Pittsburgh Tribune-Review]]|title=Quaker Valley's Adou Thiero named 2022 TribLive HSSN Boys Basketball Player of the Year|date=April 4, 2022|author=Harlan, Chris}} Thiero, born in the U.S., spent his early years in Mali with his grandmother, while his parents played college basketball. In 2007, at age three, he returned to the U.S. He attended [[Quaker Valley High School]] in [[Leetsdale, Pennsylvania]], where he played [[basketball]], [[Association football|soccer]] and [[lacrosse]].{{Cite web|url=https://ukathletics.com/sports/mbball/roster/player/adou-thiero/|publisher=[[Kentucky Wildcats]]|title=Adou Thiero|date=August 4, 2022 }} A [[combo guard]], he led Quaker Valley in scoring as a [[sophomore]], averaging 17.7 points a game. Then, as a [[Junior (education year)|junior]] in 2020–21, he remained their leading scorer and averaged 21.8 points as well as a team-leading 5.1 assists, 2.2 steals and 1.2 blocks. As a [[Senior (education)|senior]], Thiero averaged 23.3 points, 10.3 rebounds, 5.9 assists, 3.9 steals and 2.3 blocks, helping the team compile a record of 27–1 while being undefeated in league play; their only loss came in the [[Pennsylvania Interscholastic Athletic Association]] (PIAA) championship game. He set a school record with 44 points in a game, finished third in school history with 1,624 career points, and received several honors after his senior season including [[Western Pennsylvania Interscholastic Athletic League]] (WPIAL) Player of the Year, ''[[Pittsburgh Tribune-Review|TribLive HSSN]]'' Boys Basketball Player of the Year, and Pennsylvania Class 4A Player of the Year. He committed to play [[college basketball]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]], coached by John Calipari who had coached his father in college.{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3301899/2022/05/09/kentuckys-bet-on-adou-thiero-is-that-hell-embrace-the-challenge-continue-growing/|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|title=Kentucky's bet on Adou Thiero is that he'll embrace the challenge, continue growing|date=May 9, 2022|author=Tucker, Kyle}} ==College career== ===Kentucky=== As a [[freshman]] at Kentucky in 2022–23, Thiero appeared in 20 games, averaging 9.5 minutes per game, and recorded averages of 2.3 points and 1.9 rebounds.{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/college/pittsburgh/pitt-panthers-likely-missing-adou-thiero|date=May 2, 2024|author=Campbell, Dominic|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|title=Pitt Likely Missing Out on Kentucky Transfer}} He was the team leader in steals in four games and in blocks in three games. In 2023–24, he saw more playing time, appearing in 25 games, 19 as a starter, while missing eight due to injury.{{Cite news|url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article287729835.html|newspaper=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]]|title=After two seasons with Kentucky basketball, Adou Thiero is sticking with John Calipari|date=May 6, 2024|author=Drummond, Cameron}} He averaged 7.2 points and 5.0 rebounds per game, also totaling 27 blocks which was second on the team.{{Cite web|url=https://arkansas.rivals.com/news/arkansas-makes-final-cut-for-kentucky-transfer-adou-thiero|website=[[Rivals.com]]|title=Arkansas makes final cut for Kentucky transfer Adou Thiero|date=April 19, 2024|author=Choate, Mason}} He was Kentucky's leading rebounder in eight games and had five games where he scored double figures; he also posted a [[double-double]] in their game against No. 1–ranked [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], scoring 16 points and 13 rebounds. After the season, Thiero entered his name in the [[2024 NBA draft]] and the [[NCAA transfer portal]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-basketball-men/article287236985.html|date=March 30, 2024|author=Roberts, Ben|title=Adou Thiero issues statement on future. He could still return to Kentucky basketball team.}} ===Arkansas=== Thiero ended up withdrawing from the NBA draft and transferring to the [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas Razorbacks]] for the 2024–25 season, following coach Calipari who had left Kentucky.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/40094868/ex-kentucky-star-adou-thiero-joining-john-calipari-arkansas|publisher=[[ESPN]]|title=Ex-Kentucky star Adou Thiero joining John Calipari at Arkansas|date=May 6, 2024|author=Givony, Jonathan; Borzello, Jeff}} ==References== {{Reflist}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Thiero, Adou}} [[Category:2004 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Forwards (basketball)]] [[Category:Basketball players from Pennsylvania]] [[Category:Malian men's basketball players]] [[Category:Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball players]] [[Category:Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball players]]
